sources.quote: Identical wording to the 1986 book: initial-stress tendency plus penult tendency; disyllables regular (initial); polysyllables 'primary stress will usually fall on the penult and secondary stress on the first syllable'; 'a number of exceptions ... among words other than verbs, while verbs do not appear to follow it at all'; trisyllabic non-verbs 'some words follow one tendency and others the other' (/'waruke/ 'big', /'yankeyke/ 'small' vs /wiy'tape/ 'river', /yil'make/ 'moon'); suffixes do not shift stress on non-verbs; verb roots 'condition stress patterns idiosyncratically'. sources.note: Typological survey of tone vs pitch accent vs stress systems in PNG languages (word-level and syllable-level tone types). For Awtuw it draws on Feldman 1986:15ff., the word-stress section, so it most likely lists Awtuw as a stress (non-tonal) language; Second-hand; the primary source (Feldman 1986) has no tone section and describes pitch only as a correlate of word stress and of question intonation.
